subagent-stop-probe.quantity: whether the hook events see a background agent's launch and its return, and pair them (D4, D7)
subagent-stop-probe.source: a temporary user-level hook on SubagentStart, SubagentStop and PostToolUse(Agent) appending its input to the scratchpad; one background haiku agent dispatched; the hook then removed (settings restored from a copy)
subagent-stop-probe.command: the probe hook's log, read with json.loads per line
subagent-stop-probe.method: the three events' inputs read for hook_event_name, agent_type, agent_id, tool_response.status and agentId

value.SubagentStart: fired at launch: agent_type general-purpose, agent_id present
value.PostToolUse(Agent): fired at launch: tool_response.status async_launched, tool_response.agentId equal to the agent_id
value.SubagentStop: fired at the background agent's return with the same agent_id and agent_type
value.reading: a background check's return is seen by SubagentStop and paired to its dispatch through PostToolUse's agentId; D4 keeps the answer as a second return signal anyway

event-hook-cost.quantity: the event-log hook's wall time per call, beside two guards that already run on every Bash call (plan D7, Constitution Check VI)
event-hook-cost.source: the clone at the T01 draft; load average 1.2 / 1.6 / 2.4
event-hook-cost.command: 40 runs each of scripts/hooks/event-log-hooks.sh, batching-hooks.sh pretool and shell-check-hooks.sh pretool on one PreToolUse(Bash) payload, median, in a python subprocess loop
event-hook-cost.method: median wall ms of the 40; python -X importtime on event_log.py for where it goes

value.reading: inside the existing guards' range (below shell-check's); about 25 ms of it is the json and re imports. Claude Code runs a call's matching hooks in parallel, so on Bash and Edit calls it adds little wall time beside the guards already there
